classification.difficultyReason: Rewrite a constant as a logarithm, solve a radical equation and check the domain and squaring restriction.

answer.short:
$x=6$.

Combine the right-hand side as $\log_2(x)$, then solve $\sqrt{4x+1}+1=x$ and check the candidate roots.
answer.worked:
The original domain is $x>0$. Since $1=\log_2(2)$,

$$\begin{align*}\log_2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+1&=\log_2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+\log_2(2)\\\log_2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+1&=\log_2(x)\end{align*}$$

Equal logarithms with the same valid base have equal arguments.

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{4x+1}+1&=x\\\sqrt{4x+1}&=x-1\end{align*}$$

This requires $x\ge1$. Squaring gives

$$\begin{align*}(x-1)^2&=4x+1\\x^2-6x&=0\\x(x-6)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=6\end{align*}$$

Reject $x=0$, which is outside the original domain. For $x=6$, the left-hand side is $\log_2(\sqrt{25}+1)=\log_2(6)$ and the right-hand side is $\log_2(3)+1=\log_2(6)$. Hence $x=6$.
